scheme_name: Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra/Majhi Bhavan, Manki Munda Bhavan, Parha Bhavan, Pargana Bhavan, Dumkuria Bhavan Evam Gosade Nirman Tatha Majhi Than Shed Nirman Yojana
description:
The Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at promoting and preserving the cultural heritage of tribal communities. 

This scheme was officially launched on 15th August 2021. 

The primary objective of the Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is to establish cultural centers that serve as a hub for tribal art, culture, and traditions. 

These centers are designed to provide a platform for tribal artists and craftsmen to showcase their skills and promote their cultural heritage. 

The scheme aims to create at least 100 such cultural centers across various states in India by the year 2025. 

Each center is expected to facilitate workshops, exhibitions, and performances that highlight the rich traditions of tribal communities. 

In addition to cultural promotion, the scheme also seeks to empower tribal communities economically by providing them with opportunities to sell their handicrafts and artworks. 

The estimated budget allocated for the Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is approximately INR 500 crores over a span of five years. 

Each cultural center is expected to receive a funding of around INR 5 crores for its establishment and operational costs. 

The benefits of this scheme extend beyond cultural preservation. 

It is anticipated that the establishment of these centers will create job opportunities for local tribal populations. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the visibility of tribal art forms on national and international platforms. 

Eligibility for participation in the activities and benefits of the Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme primarily includes individuals from tribal communities. 

There are no specific age limits set for eligibility. 

However, participants are encouraged to have a background in traditional arts or crafts. 

The application process for individuals wishing to participate in workshops or exhibitions involves submitting a form to the respective cultural center. 

This form typically requires details such as name, age, address, and a brief description of the applicant's art or craft. 

Documents required may include proof of tribal identity, which can be a tribal certificate issued by the relevant authorities. 

The application process is designed to be straightforward to encourage maximum participation from tribal artists. 

The timeline for the establishment of the cultural centers is set to be completed by 2025. 

Disbursement of funds for the centers will occur in phases, with an initial release of 50% of the allocated budget upon approval of the center's proposal. 

The remaining funds will be released based on the performance and progress of the center in meeting its objectives. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India. 

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs can be contacted through their official website for more information regarding the scheme. 

State governments are also involved in the implementation process, ensuring that the centers are established in areas with significant tribal populations. 

The Majhi Bhavan, Manki Munda Bhavan, Parha Bhavan, Pargana Bhavan, and Dumkuria Bhavan are specific cultural centers that are part of this broader initiative. 

Each of these centers is strategically located in regions with a high concentration of tribal communities. 

These centers will serve as focal points for cultural activities and will be equipped with facilities for exhibitions and performances. 

The Majhi Bhavan is located in the state of Jharkhand and is expected to cater to the local tribal population by promoting the Santhal culture. 

The Manki Munda Bhavan is situated in Chhattisgarh and will focus on the traditions of the Gond community. 

Parha Bhavan is planned for Madhya Pradesh and will highlight the cultural practices of the Baiga tribe. 

Pargana Bhavan will be established in Odisha, showcasing the art and culture of the Kondh tribe. 

Dumkuria Bhavan will be located in West Bengal and will promote the cultural heritage of the Santal tribe. 

Each center will also collaborate with local educational institutions to conduct workshops and training sessions for the youth. 

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of pride among tribal communities regarding their cultural heritage. 

It will also facilitate the documentation of various tribal art forms, ensuring that they are preserved for future generations. 

The Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is part of a larger effort by the Indian government to uplift and empower tribal communities. 

It aligns with the goals of the Tribal Sub-Plan, which aims to ensure the socio-economic development of tribal populations. 

The government is committed to increasing the budget for tribal welfare schemes by 10% annually. 

This commitment reflects the recognition of the unique challenges faced by tribal communities in India. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the livelihoods of tribal artists by providing them with a sustainable source of income. 

By promoting tribal art and culture, the government aims to integrate these communities into the broader socio-economic framework of the country. 

The establishment of cultural centers will also serve as a means to educate the general public about the rich diversity of tribal cultures in India. 

The Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is a vital step towards ensuring that tribal communities receive the recognition and support they deserve. 

It is anticipated that the success of this scheme will lead to the replication of similar initiatives in other regions. 

The government is actively seeking partnerships with NGOs and private organizations to further enhance the impact of this scheme. 

Through these collaborative efforts, the Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme aims to create a lasting legacy for tribal cultures in India. 

The scheme represents a significant investment in the future of tribal communities and their cultural heritage. 

It is a testament to the government's commitment to inclusivity and cultural preservation. 

The Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is poised to make a meaningful difference in the lives of tribal artists and communities across India. 

It is an essential initiative that reflects the rich tapestry of India's diverse cultural landscape. 

The scheme is expected to be a game-changer in the efforts to uplift and empower tribal populations. 

Overall, the Adivasi Sanskriti Evam Kala Kendra scheme is a comprehensive approach to cultural preservation and economic empowerment for tribal communities in India.
